summary.text: A 75-year-old man with cutaneous nodular ulcerated melanoma of the left arm (BRAF wild type, Breslow thickness 2.7 mm, Clark level III) was referred to oncology in October 2018; PET showed pathological 18-FDG uptake in the liver. He was treated with intravenous pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks.

After the 10th cycle he developed itchy psoriasis over more than 30% of the body surface (PASI 12.3), which the authors call an immune-related adverse event of pembrolizumab, with a significant negative impact on quality of life and compliance, without personal history of psoriasis or autoimmune disease.

After multidisciplinary discussion he received apremilast (10 mg for 5 days, then 30 mg twice daily) and methylprednisolone 16 mg/die for 5 days with progressive reduction until discontinuation 15 days later; pembrolizumab was interrupted for 4 weeks until skin improvement and disappearance of itching.

After 10 months of treatment with apremilast and pembrolizumab he had a good clinical condition, acceptable quality of life and no relapse of psoriasis plaques, and PET and CT showed no evidence of previously described melanoma lesions (complete response per iRECIST).
